answers.how: Ball-flight curvature gives approximately 825 px/s², so the scale is 9.8/825 = 0.0119 m/px. The standing person is approximately 150 px tall.
The basket rim is approximately 266 px above the floor. Multiplying by the gravity-calibrated scale of 0.0119 m/px gives the height.
Tracking the ball around 2.00 s gives velocity components of approximately 215 px/s horizontally and 315 px/s upward. Convert their resultant using 0.0119 m/px.
Tracking the ball around 3.00 s gives approximately 193 px/s horizontally and 505 px/s downward. Convert their resultant using 0.0119 m/px.
At 3.00 s, the ball center and basket rim center are separated by approximately 151 px, equivalent to 1.80 m.
At 3.00 s, the person’s center and ball center are approximately 270 px apart. Apply the gravity-calibrated scale.
At 4.00 s, the ball center is approximately 169 px above the floor level inferred from its bounces. Apply 0.0119 m/px.
The person moves approximately 176 px over 1.50 s. Converting this displacement with 0.0119 m/px and dividing by elapsed time gives the average walking speed.
The ball moves from approximately (325,146) px to (631,230) px. Its displacement magnitude is approximately 317 px, converted using 0.0119 m/px.
